data.name: Jubilee
data.gender_notes: Jubilee is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In the Bible, a jubilee is a year of rest and forgiveness. The Hebrew word for jubilee, 'yobel', comes from a ram's horn, which was blown to announce the start of the year. This name is a reminder of God's promise to forgive and renew. The name Jubilee carries the meaning “Year of Jubilee” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Jubilee usually hope their child will grow to embody year of jubilee and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Jubilee belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Year of Jubilee.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jubilee total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_english.name: Jubilee
in_english.meaning: festival of freedom, celebration of liberation, joyful occasion, happy time, time of rejoicing
in_english.long_meaning: The name Jubilee originates from the Hebrew words יאגמרב (Σλοππώμεάλι) and ובויב (σετπυ γόλείας). It refers to the 50th year in the Hebrew calendar, when debts were forgiven, slaves were freed, and land was returned to its original owners. In Christianity, the concept of Jubilee is associated with the idea of spiritual freedom and liberation, where believers are freed from sin and bondage to live a life of joy and freedom in Christ.

data.cultural_impact: The Christian concept of a "Jubilee year" is derived from the Jewish tradition of Sabbath years, when land was allowed to lie fallow, debts were forgiven, and freedom was granted to slaves and prisoners. Celebrating a Jubilee year in Christianity signifies a call to rest, reflection, and renewal in all areas of life.
data.spiritual_significance: A Jubilee year is a powerful reminder of God's mercy and compassion. In the Bible, during a Jubilee year, the trumpet's blast was a call to return to the sanctuary and to God. It symbolizes a spiritual wash and renewal of the soul, offering forgiveness, restoration, and the opportunity for a fresh start. It mirrors the essence of Christianity - God's love, forgiveness, mercy, and continuous renewal.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The Biblical Jubilee year signifies freedom, release from debt, and restoration. In a spiritual sense, it represents God's merciful forgiveness and liberation from bondage, inviting believers to start anew with a clean slate.

biblical_reference.note: The concept of Jubilee is introduced in Leviticus 25:8-55, where God commands the Israelites to observe a year of jubilee every 50 years, when all debts are forgiven, slaves are freed, and land is returned to its original owners.

historical_references.reference: The Jubilee Year was a year of special religious significance in the Hebrew calendar. It occurred every 50 years and was proclaimed by the high priest during the Feast of Trumpets, a holy day. The year was marked by the blowing of trumpets, the release of prisoners, and the return of land to its original owners or their heirs. This practice was based on Leviticus 25:8-13.

The term 'Jubilee' was adopted by Christians to refer to a year of reconciliation and forgiveness. It was first used in the 15th century during the Jubilee Year of 1450, declared by Pope Callixtus III. The year was marked by the granting of indulgences, the release of prisoners, and the permission for serfs to leave their lords' lands. This practice was influenced by the Jewish concept of the Jubilee Year and the Christian belief in the Year of Jubilee as described in Leviticus 25.

modern_usage.modern_context: The modern context of the Christian name 'Jubilee' refers to several concepts and movements that have emerged in various spheres of life. This biblical term is often associated with the cancellation of debts, celebration of renewal, return to community, and spiritual renewal. In the context of Christian faith, Jubilee is observed as a time of forgiveness and release from sins, debts, and other burdens. In the realm of economics, Jubilee Economics is a movement advocating for debt cancellation and economic justice. Lastly, in the broader society, the concept of a Jubilee Year is often used to mark significant milestones and call for renewal and restoration, such as a nation's centennial anniversary. This timeless concept continues to inspire individuals and communities to seek forgiveness, renewal, and restoration in various aspects of life.
